title: 시장 과일 가게에서: 이거 얼마예요?
objective: Ask prices with '이거 얼마예요?', understand prices like '한 개에 ○원', order with '주세요 / -만 주세요', and ask '카드 돼요?' or '계좌이체 돼요?'.
summary: A short conversation at a Korean market fruit stall: ask prices, order, and ask how to pay.
setting: A fruit stall in a traditional market. A customer points at a basket of apples and talks with the stall owner.

task.title: COMPLETE THE MARKET PHRASES
task.line: Use the dialogue and the word list to fill in or choose the missing part of each sentence.

words.meaning: counter for pieces or items (used after a number)
per, for (after an amount, when you give a price)
words.exampleMeaning: Korean melons are 5,000 won for three.

words.meaning: please give me; I'll take (when ordering)
is accepted, is okay (when asking about payment)

words.exampleMeaning: I'll send it by bank transfer.

dialogue.meaning: Excuse me (to the owner), how much is this?
The apples? They're 10,000 won a basket.

dialogue.korean: 복숭아는 한 개에 삼천 원, 세 개에 팔천 원이에요.
dialogue.meaning: Peaches are 3,000 won each, or 8,000 won for three.

dialogue.korean: 그럼 사과 한 바구니 주세요. 복숭아는 두 개만 주세요.
dialogue.meaning: Then I'll take one basket of apples. And just two peaches, please.
Card is fine, and bank transfer is fine too.
Then I'll pay by bank transfer.

exercises: Choose the particle that means 'per': 사과 한 바구니(에 / 를) 만 원이에요.
Look at the dialogue. How much are three peaches? Fill in the blank: 복숭아는 세 개에 ____ 원이에요.
Fill in the blank to ask the price of the fruit right in front of you: ____ 얼마예요?
You want only two peaches. Fill in the blank: 복숭아는 두 개____ 주세요.
Ask if you can pay by card. Fill in the blank: 카드 ____?
